# Vegetation Encroachment Risk

Vegetation Encroachment Risk assesses how nearby plant growth raises the chance of power outages by interfering with utility lines. It quantifies the probability that branches or foliage within a defined buffer zone will cause faults, factoring in species growth rates, weather patterns, and historical incident data. The system integrates camera network imagery with line inspection records to update risk scores monthly.

Tradeoffs include balancing thorough coverage with processing costs and false positives from transient vegetation like vines. For example, a 15-meter span near a 12 kV line with fast-growing willow trees may have a 0.08 monthly outage risk, doubling from 0.04 if not trimmed after six months. Common failures involve obscured camera views, delayed inspections, and misclassifying non-threatening plants as risks.
